Small Condo Association Management in Chicago.

A smaller building still has legal obligations, shared assets, vendor contracts, reserves, and owner expectations. CenterPoint gives volunteer boards a professional operating system without treating the community like a number.

Professional structure without big-firm distance.

Small associations often run well until a major repair, delinquency, insurance renewal, difficult rule dispute, or board turnover exposes the limits of volunteer systems. Professional management should not remove the board’s authority; it should give directors better records, reliable execution, and enough time to govern.

Volunteer overload

Replace scattered owner spreadsheets, inboxes, and verbal handoffs with an operating calendar, documented responsibilities, and one accountable manager.

Financial blind spots

Build board-ready budgets and monthly reports, track receivables, preserve invoice support, and make reserve needs visible before a project becomes an emergency.

Vendor dependence

Create clear scopes, obtain comparable bids, verify insurance, document approvals, and keep service history available to future boards.

Inconsistent enforcement

Use the declaration, bylaws, rules, notices, and hearing process consistently so decisions are documented and defensible.

Deferred maintenance

Turn roofs, masonry, porches, plumbing, and shared mechanical systems into planned work instead of recurring owner emergencies.

Board turnover

Keep records, contracts, decisions, owner balances, and open issues in a durable system that does not leave when a director’s term ends.

Full-service association management, right-sized.

  • Condominium associations and vintage conversions, not apartment rentals
  • A dedicated manager and direct board communication
  • Full-service financial, governance, maintenance, and owner support
  • Flat-fee proposals starting at $20 per unit per month
  • A managed transition from self-management or another company

A transition that protects the board’s institutional memory.

For a self-managed association, onboarding begins with a records inventory: governing documents, bank authority, owner ledger, contracts, insurance, tax and corporate records, meeting minutes, warranties, keys, open violations, and planned work. We then establish the annual calendar and move routine administration into systems the whole board can see.

For an association leaving another manager, CenterPoint coordinates the 30-60 day handoff and tracks missing items until the record is complete. The result is continuity for owners and a clean starting point for the incoming board-manager partnership.

What small condo boards ask before hiring management.

Clear scope, clear pricing, and a transition plan your board can evaluate before making a decision.

Does CenterPoint work with small and boutique condominium associations?

Yes. CenterPoint provides full-service association management for small Chicago condo buildings and vintage conversions as well as larger communities. The service is for condominium associations, not rental apartments.

Can a small association afford professional management?

Pricing starts at $20 per unit per month, with a customized flat monthly proposal based on the actual scope. The board can compare the fee with the time, continuity, reporting, collections, vendor, maintenance, and compliance responsibilities currently carried by volunteers.

What problems does management solve for a self-managed condo?

Professional management replaces scattered inboxes, spreadsheets, and verbal handoffs with board-ready financials, owner ledgers, insured-vendor records, meeting and decision documentation, a maintenance calendar, consistent communications, and records that survive board turnover.

Will the board still control decisions?

Yes. The board retains its governing authority. CenterPoint organizes information, carries out authorized work, tracks deadlines, and gives directors a dependable operating system so they can make and document decisions more effectively.

How does a small association transition to CenterPoint?

Onboarding begins with a records inventory and a 30-60 day handoff covering governing documents, banking, owner balances, contracts, insurance, tax and corporate records, minutes, warranties, keys, open issues, and planned work.
